**Synopsis:**
Fed Governor Waller signals a conditional hold at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, contingent on August CPI data showing continued disinflation progress. He leaves a rate hike explicitly on the table if inflation re-accelerates. The current policy rate sits at 3.50%-3.75%, described as only mildly restrictive. Upside inflation risks flagged include elevated energy prices, AI-driven tech goods price pressures, and potential additional tariffs. Fed Chair Warsh (Jackson Hole) had previously tilted hawkish. Market pricing shifted post-remarks to ~50/50 on a September hike, down from ~60%.

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: Is it striking a different sentiment/tone compared to previous discussions on US interest rates?**
Difference: -20 (Modestly more dovish than the immediately preceding tone — Warsh at Jackson Hole leaned hawkish, and market pricing was at ~60% hike pre-remarks; Waller's conditional hold language shifted odds to ~50/50, representing a slight dovish relief relative to the prevailing hawkish consensus, though the hike option remains live)

**Q06. Focus on the very latest information: How does it compare to previous information on US interest rates?**
Difference: -20 (Same read — Waller's "willing to hold" framing is a mild dovish tilt versus the recent Fed communication drift, which had been predominantly hawkish. The explicit hike threat keeps this from being materially dovish. Net: a minor dovish recalibration, not a pivot.)
